subject: ILCE-6400 SA updater-crypto registry boundary

observations.source: CX62600_ALLLANG.bin filename slots and eight-byte registry records
observations.claim: The unique sa_aes_sha2.bin filename is slot 54 and record 54 is the four-word tuple [54, 147, 19, 1].
The container has the observed magic, identity SA_AESSH0x01, module AES_SHA20x01, and big-endian header words [19, 1].

observations.source: sa_udrt.bin registry record and outer header
observations.claim: The unique sa_udrt.bin filename is slot 91, its record is [91, 147, 63, 1], and its observed container header words are [63, 1].

unresolved.source: Static cross-reference search of currently extracted updater and camera components
unresolved.claim: No verified updater path has been found that invokes either registered program; registry type 147 and program IDs 19 and 63 do not establish a caller.

unresolved.source: Custom SA instruction image and unavailable public ISA tooling
unresolved.claim: The secure-application ABI, any relationship to firmware payload processing, and any relationship between SA program ID 63 and the separate IMDB entry ID 63 remain unknown.

conclusion: The AES/SHA and UDRT secure applications are registered by the alpha 6400 runtime, but registration and matching numeric values across separate tables do not prove updater invocation, firmware processing, or a usable cryptographic boundary.
